subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Enzymes speed up reactions by:
questions.explain: Enzymes provide an alternative pathway with lower activation energy; they do not change the reaction's equilibrium.

questions.q: The region of an enzyme where the substrate binds is the:
questions.explain: The active site has a specific shape and chemistry complementary to its substrate.

questions.q: The induced-fit model proposes that on substrate binding the active site:
options: Changes shape slightly to fit the substrate more closely
questions.explain: Induced fit refines the older 'lock and key' idea: binding causes a conformational change that strains bonds and aids catalysis.

questions.q: Raising temperature above an enzyme's optimum decreases the reaction rate because it:
options: Denatures the enzyme, altering the active site
questions.explain: Excess heat breaks the bonds maintaining tertiary structure, so the active site no longer fits the substrate.

questions.q: A competitive inhibitor reduces enzyme activity by:
options: Binding to the active site and blocking the substrate
Binding away from the active site and changing its shape
questions.explain: Competitive inhibitors resemble the substrate and compete for the active site; their effect can be overcome by more substrate.

questions.q: Reactions that build larger molecules from smaller ones, requiring energy, are described as:
questions.explain: Anabolism builds complex molecules (e.g. protein synthesis); catabolism breaks them down (e.g. digestion).

questions.q: The universal short-term energy currency of cells is:
questions.explain: ATP releases usable energy when its terminal phosphate bond is hydrolysed to ADP + Pi.

questions.q: In eukaryotes, glycolysis takes place in the:
questions.explain: Glycolysis, splitting glucose into two pyruvate molecules, occurs in the cytoplasm and does not require oxygen.

questions.q: The Krebs cycle occurs in the:
questions.explain: The link reaction and Krebs cycle take place in the matrix; oxidative phosphorylation occurs on the inner membrane (cristae).

questions.q: In aerobic respiration, the final acceptor of electrons in the electron transport chain is:
questions.explain: Oxygen accepts electrons and combines with hydrogen to form water; without it the chain and ATP synthesis stop.

questions.q: In human muscle during vigorous exercise, anaerobic respiration produces:
questions.explain: Human anaerobic respiration converts pyruvate to lactate, regenerating NAD+ so glycolysis can continue; yeast instead produce ethanol and CO2.

questions.q: The light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis occur in the:
questions.explain: Light-dependent reactions occur in the thylakoids; the light-independent (Calvin) cycle occurs in the stroma.

questions.q: During the light-dependent reactions, the oxygen released comes from:
questions.explain: Photolysis splits water into electrons, protons and oxygen; the oxygen is a by-product released to the atmosphere.

questions.q: The light-independent (Calvin) cycle fixes which molecule into organic compounds?
questions.explain: CO2 is fixed using ATP and NADPH from the light reactions to build carbohydrates.

questions.q: On a graph, increasing light intensity raises the rate of photosynthesis until it plateaus. At the plateau the rate is limited by:
options: Another factor such as CO2 concentration or temperature
The number of chloroplasts fixed forever
questions.explain: At the plateau light is no longer limiting; a different factor (often CO2 or temperature) becomes the limiting factor.

questions.q: The main photosynthetic pigment that absorbs mostly red and blue light (reflecting green) is:
questions.explain: Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue wavelengths and reflects green, giving leaves their colour; its absorption spectrum matches the action spectrum.

questions.q: When substrate concentration is very high and all active sites are occupied, the enzyme reaction rate:
questions.explain: At saturation, adding more substrate cannot increase the rate because every enzyme is already working.

questions.q: The complete oxidation of one glucose molecule in aerobic respiration yields far more ATP than anaerobic respiration because:
options: The electron transport chain and oxygen allow much more ATP to be produced
questions.explain: Aerobic respiration (~30–38 ATP) far exceeds the 2 ATP net from anaerobic glycolysis.

questions.q: ATP and NADPH produced in the light-dependent reactions are used in the Calvin cycle to:
options: Reduce fixed carbon dioxide into carbohydrate
questions.explain: The Calvin cycle uses this chemical energy and reducing power to convert CO2 into sugars.

questions.q: Metabolism as a whole is best described as:
options: The sum of all enzyme-controlled reactions in an organism
The movement of substances across membranes
questions.explain: Metabolism includes both anabolic and catabolic pathways, organised into linked reaction sequences.
